title: x-control
description: A security control from any publisher, with its specification, guidance, lifecycle state, and source provenance. Defined by the CSA Security Controls Catalog. See SCHEMA-STIX-OBJECT-EXTENSIONS.md for narrative definitions.

framework_namespace.description: Publisher namespace, mirroring the SecID namespace component (e.g. cloudsecurityalliance.org, iso.org, nist.gov).

framework.description: Framework name, mirroring the SecID name component (e.g. ccm, aicm, 27001, 800-53).

framework_version.description: Framework edition, mirroring the SecID @version component. Optional: some sources are unversioned.

control_identifier.description: The publisher's own identifier for the control, mirroring the SecID subpath (e.g. CEK-03, A.8.24, AC-1).

status.description: Catalog lifecycle. Orthogonal to the standard STIX revoked property, which means withdrawn as invalid. Never express retirement with revoked.

specification.description: The control requirement. Holds reproduced text and is therefore licence-constrained: populate only where the source permits reproduction. See CONVENTIONS-STIX-MODELING.md section 8.

stack_components.description: Architectural layers the control applies to, carried as the layers that apply rather than a map of every layer to true or false. Omitted when none apply: STIX prohibits empty lists, so an empty array and an absent property are the same thing on the wire and the schema rejects the empty form rather than letting it mean something it cannot mean.

lifecycle_relevance.description: Lifecycle phases in which the control applies, each mapped to the sub-phases that apply within it. A phase with no named sub-phases may be null. Phase names are the publisher's. Carried as the phases that apply, and omitted when none do: STIX prohibits empty dictionaries, so the schema rejects the empty form.

object_marking_refs.description: Data markings applying to the whole object. Every catalog object carries TLP:WHITE, since the catalog is public. TLP:WHITE is the STIX 2.1 spelling of what TLP 2.0 renamed TLP:CLEAR; the identifier is assigned by the specification, and STIX forbids producers from defining their own tlp markings. Additional markings may be present.

control_type.description: The publisher's classification of the control. AICM 1.0.3 uses 'Cloud & AI Related', 'AI-Specific', and 'Cloud-Specific'. Not enumerated here: other frameworks classify differently, and the charter's Control Data Model leaves the vocabulary open.

threat_category.description: Threat categories the control addresses, from the publisher's own threat taxonomy. Carried as the categories that apply rather than a map of every category to true or false, which is lossless and filterable. Omitted when none apply, since STIX prohibits empty lists. These are a taxonomy applied to the control, not objects in the catalog, so they are a property rather than relationships — if threats become first-class objects, mitigates relationships would complement this.

typical_control_applicability_and_owners.description: Which architectural layer the control applies to, mapped to who owns it there — for example 'Owned by the Model Provider (MP)' or 'Shared CSP-MP'. One field rather than separate applicability and ownership properties, because ownership varies by layer and the pairing is the information.

implementation_guidelines.description: How to fulfill the control, keyed by responsible role. Role sets are framework-specific — AICM uses six including model_provider and ai_customer, CCM uses csp, csc, and shared — so the keys are open. Use 'shared' for guidance that is not role-specific. Holds reproduced text and is therefore licence-constrained.

auditing_guidelines.description: How to audit the control, keyed by responsible role, on the same basis as implementation_guidelines. Holds reproduced text and is therefore licence-constrained.

valid_from.description: When the thing this object describes became valid — a standard's publication date, or when a mapping was first asserted. Distinct from created, which is when this record was written: an object minted in 2026 may describe a standard valid from 2013.

valid_until.description: When it stopped being current. Present on a superseded object, so historical questions stay answerable — what was current as of a given date — while signalling that new work should use the successor. May be in the future, for an announced transition, in which case the object is still current until then. Absent means still current. Not a substitute for revoked: valid_until says the claim held until a date, revoked says it should never have been relied on.

allOf.$comment: Citation-only sources. Where a publisher's terms do not permit reproduction, the object carries the standard number and the clause identifier and no prose at all — no title, no excerpt, no paraphrase. This is the same minimum CCM and AICM use when citing these sources. ISO/IEC is the named absolute case and is enforced here; the authoritative test for any other source is its SecID licence record, which this check does not replace. See CONVENTIONS-STIX-MODELING.md section 8.

newSdoExtension.description: Declares the object as a new SDO defined by a CSA extension-definition. The definition object must travel with the instance in any published bundle.
